meta.shellLabel: Module 1 · Lesson 3 · Keep Some Money Aside
meta.skillName: Choose to Keep Some Money Instead of Spending It All
meta.learningOutcome: I understand the basics of money changes over time
meta.conceptTruth: Money doesn’t have to be spent - it can be kept and used in more beneficial ways
meta.behaviourShift:
From spending all remaining money on wants once needs are covered
 → To choosing to keep some money because it can be used in better ways than immediate spending
meta.ruleEnforcement: I don’t spend everything - I always keep some aside

baseScreens.prompt: Mia borrowed her sister's headphones and broke them. What happened next?

optionA.label: Mia has no money to buy a new pair

optionB.label: Mia tries to fix them with sticky tape and now they're even worse

baseScreens.wrongError: Haha, maybe. But let's try again

authoring.contentForGame:
- Mia has no money to buy a new pair
- Mia tries to fix them with sticky tape and now they're even worse
- the dog runs off with one of the pieces
authoring.errorMessage:
Option 1 = correct.
Message if submitted correct: "Exactly! No money left = big sister drama."
If submitted incorrect answer: "Haha, maybe. But let's try again"

baseScreens.intro: Mia had $40. Drag each purchase into Spent to see what's left for her sister's headphones.
baseScreens.successMessage: Mia has no money left to pay for new headphones

authoring.contentForGame:
Screen Layout:

Left Side (Inventory): Three distinct icons representing Mia's recent purchases:

A Squishy toy (+ icon) $25
A Slime (+ tub icon). $8
Snacks (chocolate bar/wrapper icon). $7

Right Side (The bucket/bin): A target area labeled [Spent].
Dynamic Counter (Bottom): A digital display: Total Spent: $0 / $40

Screen starts with '$40 available' and each time an item is dragged to 'spent' the 'amount available' drops by the value of that item.
authoring.errorMessage: When all items are dragged and the 'amount available' hits $0 a pop up shows the message: "Mia has no money left to pay for new headphones"

authoring.contentForGame:
What should Mia do?

[Buy the toy and save $10 more next week.] (The Trap)
[Buy the headphones to fix what she broke.] (The Concept Truth)
[Buy the toy and hope the headphones don't cost $40.] (The Trap)

If #2: "Smart move. Replacing the broken headphones should come first."

baseScreens.narrativeAfter: everything, I had Spare Cash to replace the headphones immediately.
baseScreens.wrongError: Think about what Mia did — she didn't use all her money.

authoring.contentForGame: "Because I didn't ['spend' = correct answer / save = wrong answer] everything, I had ['Spare Cash' = correct/ 'Borrowed money' = incorrect] to ['replace' = good / 'throw away' = bad] the headphones immediately."

baseScreens.narrative: Exactly! Keeping some money means you’re in charge, you don't have to beg for cash, and you can get the stuff that actually matters.
